# 1. Executive Summary (~250 words)

[Organization Name] requests $[amount] over [number] [months/years] to [verb: launch / expand / strengthen] [program name], a [brief descriptor, e.g., "community-based behavioral health intervention"] serving [number] [population, e.g., "transition-age youth aged 18–24"] in [city/county/region]. [Program name] will deliver three core activities: [Activity 1, e.g., "intensive case management"], [Activity 2, e.g., "peer-led skills workshops"], and [Activity 3, e.g., "coordinated referral to partner agencies"]. Each participant will receive [dosage, e.g., "a minimum of 12 weeks of structured support"], moving through a clear pathway from intake and assessment through active services and follow-up.

By the end of the grant period, the program will achieve the following measurable outcomes: [X]% of participants will [primary outcome, e.g., "obtain stable housing"], up from a baseline of [Y]%, and [X]% will [secondary outcome, e.g., "report improved self-efficacy"], as measured by [validated tool or method]. We expect to serve [number] individuals [annually / over the grant period] at a cost of $[amount] per participant, [comparison phrase, e.g., "well below the regional average of $[amount] for comparable programs (source)"].

[Organization Name] brings [number] years of experience delivering [related services] in [community], supported by [key asset, e.g., "a multilingual staff," "established referral partnerships with [number] agencies," or "a track record of [result]"]. [Matching/leveraged funds sentence, e.g., "The organization is committing $[amount] in matching funds and in-kind support to ensure program sustainability beyond the grant period."]

# 2. Statement of Need (~600 words)

## The Problem

[City/County/Region] faces a persistent and growing [problem, e.g., "gap in accessible behavioral health services for young adults"]. Despite [contextual factor, e.g., "a population increase of [X]% since [year] (source)"], the supply of [relevant service] has [remained flat / declined / failed to keep pace], leaving [population] without adequate support during a critical period of [developmental stage / economic transition / health vulnerability].

The consequences are measurable. According to [source, year], [X]% of [population] in [geographic area] [experience condition, e.g., "reported a major depressive episode in the past year"], a rate [X] times [higher than / above] the [state / national] average of [Y]% ([source, year]). [Second data point: e.g., "Emergency department visits for [condition] among [age group] in [county] rose [X]% between [year] and [year] ([source])."]. [Third data point, ideally local: e.g., "The [school district / health department / police department] recorded [number] [incidents / referrals / reports] in [year], up from [number] in [year] ([source])."]

This is not a new trend. [Brief trend sentence, e.g., "[Indicator] has worsened steadily over the past [number] years, with the sharpest increase occurring between [year] and [year] ([source])."]. Without intervention, projections suggest [consequence, e.g., "the number of [population] experiencing [condition] will reach [number] by [year] ([source, if available])"].

## Service Gaps

Existing resources in [area] are insufficient to meet the scale of the need. [Gap statement 1, e.g., "The nearest [type of provider] is [distance / travel time] from [neighborhood], and currently operates at [X]% capacity with a waitlist of [number] individuals ([source / internal data, date])."]. [Gap statement 2, e.g., "[Number] of the [total number] licensed [providers] in [county] accept [Medicaid / uninsured patients], creating a significant access barrier for the [X]% of our target population who are [uninsured / publicly insured] ([source, year])."]. [Gap statement 3 — programmatic gap, e.g., "Available programs focus primarily on [crisis / acute care], with no local option providing the [sustained, wraparound, preventive] support that research identifies as most effective for this population ([cite evidence base])."]

## Community Voice

Quantitative data alone does not capture the urgency residents feel. In [month, year], [Organization Name] conducted [method, e.g., "a community needs assessment survey"] with [number] [residents / participants / families] in [area]. [Finding 1, e.g., "[X]% of respondents identified [problem] as one of their top three concerns."]. [Finding 2, e.g., "Participants described [barrier], with one respondent noting, '[brief, representative quote].'"]. [Finding 3, e.g., "[X]% said they had sought [service] in the past [timeframe] but were unable to access it due to [barrier] ([internal report, year])."]

These findings are consistent with priorities identified by [external body, e.g., "the [County] Community Health Improvement Plan ([year])"], which lists [problem] as a top-tier strategic priority for [year–year].

The need is clear, documented, and growing. [Program Name] is designed to close the specific gaps outlined above by providing [brief bridge to Section 4, e.g., "accessible, evidence-informed services embedded in the neighborhoods where [population] already live and seek help"].

Within this community, [population] face particular vulnerability. # 4. Program Design & Activities (~800 words)

## Approach and Evidence Base

[Program Name] uses a [descriptor, e.g., "trauma-informed, strengths-based"] service model grounded in [evidence base, e.g., "the [named framework / intervention model] developed by [originator] ([citation, year])"]. Research demonstrates that [core mechanism, e.g., "sustained, relationship-driven case management paired with structured skill-building"] produces [outcome, e.g., "significant improvements in [indicator] among [population]"] ([source, year]; [source, year]). Our design adapts this evidence to the local context described in Section 2 by [adaptation, e.g., "embedding services in community sites already frequented by participants, delivering content in [languages], and integrating peer support to reduce stigma"].

The program rests on a clear theory of change: if [population] receive [inputs — services, duration, intensity], then [short-term outcomes] will occur, leading to [long-term outcomes], because [mechanism / rationale]. A one-page logic model is included as Attachment [letter/number]; the narrative below walks through each component.

## Logic Model Summary

**Inputs → Activities → Outputs → Short-Term Outcomes → Long-Term Outcomes**

**Inputs:** [Organization] staff ([number] FTE), grant funds ($[amount]), partner commitments from [partner names], physical space at [location(s)], and [other key resource, e.g., "validated curriculum materials"].

**Activity 1 — [Name, e.g., "Individualized Case Management"]**
Each participant will be assigned a dedicated [role, e.g., "Case Manager"] who conducts a comprehensive intake assessment using [tool name] and develops an individualized service plan within [timeframe, e.g., "the first two weeks of enrollment"]. The Case Manager will maintain a caseload of no more than [number] participants and will meet with each participant [frequency, e.g., "weekly for 60-minute sessions"] for a minimum of [duration, e.g., "16 weeks"]. Sessions focus on [content areas, e.g., "goal-setting, barrier identification, resource navigation, and crisis planning"].
**Output:** [number] participants receive [number] hours of one-on-one case management [annually / per cohort].
**Linked outcomes:** [X]% of participants will [outcome, e.g., "achieve at least [number] of [number] individualized service-plan goals"] by program exit, as measured by [tool / record review].

**Activity 2 — [Name, e.g., "Peer-Led Skills Workshops"]**
Participants will attend [frequency, e.g., "twice-weekly, 90-minute"] group workshops facilitated by [role, e.g., "a trained Peer Specialist and a licensed [credential] clinician"]. The curriculum spans [number] sessions organized into [number] modules: [Module 1 name, e.g., "Financial Literacy"], [Module 2 name, e.g., "Health and Wellness"], and [Module 3 name, e.g., "Communication and Conflict Resolution"]. The curriculum is adapted from [evidence-based curriculum name] ([source, year]), which has demonstrated [result] in [comparable population].
**Output:** [number] workshop sessions delivered per [year / cohort]; average participant attendance of [X]% or higher.
**Linked outcomes:** [X]% of participants will [outcome, e.g., "demonstrate a statistically significant increase in [skill / knowledge domain]"] as measured by pre/post administration of [assessment tool].

**Activity 3 — [Name, e.g., "Coordinated Referral and Follow-Up"]**
[Organization] maintains formal referral agreements with [number] partner agencies (see attached MOUs) spanning [service categories, e.g., "housing, employment, primary care, and legal aid"]. The [role, e.g., "Resource Navigator"] will facilitate warm hand-offs — accompanying participants to initial appointments when needed — and will track referral completion through [system, e.g., "[database / shared platform]"]. Follow-up contact occurs at [intervals, e.g., "30, 60, and 90 days post-referral"] to confirm service engagement and address emerging barriers.
**Output:** [number] referrals completed per [year / cohort]; [X]% confirmed linkage rate.
**Linked outcomes:** [X]% of referred participants will [outcome, e.g., "remain engaged with the referred service at the 90-day follow-up point"], up from a current baseline of [Y]% ([source / internal data, year]).

## Participant Pathway

Participants move through four sequential phases. **Phase 1 — Outreach and Enrollment ([weeks, e.g., "Weeks 1–2"]):** [Organization] recruits participants through [channels, e.g., "partner referrals, community events, social media, and walk-ins"]. Prospective participants complete an eligibility screening and, upon enrollment, receive an orientation covering program expectations, rights, and confidentiality. **Phase 2 — Assessment and Planning ([weeks, e.g., "Weeks 2–4"]):** The Case Manager administers [assessment tools] and collaborates with the participant to develop an individualized service plan with measurable goals. **Phase 3 — Active Services ([weeks, e.g., "Weeks 4–18"]):** Participants engage concurrently in Activities 1, 2, and 3. The Case Manager reviews progress biweekly and adjusts the service plan as needed. **Phase 4 — Transition and Follow-Up ([weeks, e.g., "Weeks 18–24"]):** Services taper as participants meet goals. The team completes exit assessments, secures ongoing community linkages, and schedules [number] post-exit check-ins at [intervals] to track sustained outcomes.

This phased design ensures that intensity matches participant need, that no one exits without a support plan, and that outcome data capture both immediate gains and longer-term retention.

# 6. Outcomes & Objectives (~400 words)

## Distinguishing Outputs from Outcomes

[Program Name] tracks both outputs (the volume of services delivered) and outcomes (the measurable changes participants experience as a result). The objectives below focus on outcomes. Output targets — including [number] participants enrolled, [number] case management hours delivered, [number] workshop sessions held, and [number] referrals completed — are detailed in the logic model (Attachment [letter/number]) and will be reported quarterly.

## SMART Objectives

Each objective is specific, measurable, achievable, relevant, and time-bound, and ties directly to a core activity described in Section 4.

**Objective 1 — [Domain, e.g., "Service Plan Goal Attainment"] (linked to Activity 1: [Case Management])**
By [end of grant period / Month 12], [target %] of participants who complete the program will achieve at least [number] of [number] individualized service-plan goals, up from a baseline of [baseline %] among comparable clients served in [prior year / prior program] ([internal data, year]). Progress will be measured through quarterly service-plan reviews documented in [data system].

**Objective 2 — [Domain, e.g., "Knowledge and Skill Gains"] (linked to Activity 2: [Workshops])**
By [end of each cohort cycle / Month X], [target %] of workshop participants will demonstrate a statistically significant increase in [skill / knowledge domain, e.g., "financial literacy" / "coping self-efficacy"] as measured by pre/post administration of [tool name, e.g., "the [Validated Scale] ([author, year])"], compared with a baseline mean score of [baseline score] recorded at intake.

**Objective 3 — [Domain, e.g., "Sustained Service Linkage"] (linked to Activity 3: [Referral & Follow-Up])**
By [Month 12 / end of grant period], [target %] of participants referred to partner services will remain engaged with the referred provider at the 90-day follow-up point, up from a current confirmed linkage rate of [baseline %] ([internal data, year]). Engagement will be verified through [method, e.g., "partner confirmation via shared tracking platform and participant self-report"].

**Objective 4 — [Domain, e.g., "Participant Well-Being"] (cross-cutting, linked to Activities 1–3)**
By program exit, [target %] of participants will report improved [well-being indicator, e.g., "overall mental health status"], defined as a [number]-point or greater improvement on the [tool name, e.g., "[Validated Screening Instrument]"] ([author, year]), from a baseline mean of [baseline score] collected at intake.

These four objectives capture the program's intended impact across individual goal attainment, skill acquisition, system navigation, and holistic well-being, providing the funder and the community with a comprehensive picture of effectiveness.

# 7. Evaluation Plan (~400 words)

## Design

[Organization Name] will conduct a [design type, e.g., "pre-post, single-group longitudinal"] evaluation of [Program Name]. Data will be collected at four structured points: intake, mid-point ([Month/Week X]), program exit, and [number]-day post-exit follow-up. This design allows the evaluation team to measure within-participant change over time and to assess whether gains are sustained after services conclude.

## Measurement Methods and Tools

Each objective is paired with a specific measurement method.

| Objective | Indicator | Tool / Data Source | Collection Points |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1. Service-plan goal attainment | % of participants meeting ≥[number] goals | Service-plan review in [data system] | Quarterly and at exit |
| 2. Knowledge and skill gains | Mean score change on [scale name] | [Validated Scale] ([author, year]), administered on paper / digitally | Intake and exit (pre/post) |
| 3. Sustained service linkage | % engaged at 90 days post-referral | Partner confirmation log and participant self-report via [method, e.g., "phone follow-up"] | 30-day and 90-day post-referral |
| 4. Participant well-being | Mean score change on [screening instrument] | [Validated Instrument] ([author, year]) | Intake, mid-point, exit, and [number]-day post-exit |

All instruments will be administered in [languages] to reflect the linguistic profile of the target population. Participant consent and data privacy protections comply with [applicable standards, e.g., "HIPAA," "42 CFR Part 2," "IRB exemption determination from [institution]"].

## Staffing and Frequency

The [Data / Evaluation Coordinator] ([X] FTE) is responsible for data entry, quality assurance checks, and preliminary analysis. [He/She/They] will run monthly completeness reports to flag missing records and will prepare quarterly dashboards for the [Program Manager]. [Organization Name] has contracted with [external evaluator name, if applicable] to conduct [annual / end-of-grant] analysis and to produce a final evaluation report, ensuring independent review of findings. If no external evaluator is engaged, the [Director of Programs] will review all analyses to maintain objectivity.

## Continuous Improvement and Dissemination

Evaluation is not an end-of-grant exercise; it drives real-time program refinement. The [Program Manager] will convene a quarterly review meeting with all program staff to examine participant-level data, identify trends such as attendance drop-off or uneven goal attainment, and adjust service delivery accordingly. Changes made as a result of data review will be documented in quarterly reports to [funder name].

Findings will be shared with three audiences: the funder, through required progress and final reports; program participants, through an accessible annual summary distributed at [community event / advisory meeting]; and the broader field, through [method, e.g., "presentation at [conference name]" or "publication on [Organization]'s website"]. This commitment to transparency ensures accountability to the community described in Section 2 and contributes to the evidence base for [program model / issue area].
